doc_name: List of directors of the Metropolitan Museum of Art
text: The Director of the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City, commonly known as "the Met," is the highest-ranking official and oversees the museum's operations. The Met is the largest art museum in the United States and, in 2018, attracted 6,953,927 visitors, making it the third most visited art museum in the world. Its permanent collection comprises over two million works, organized across seventeen curatorial departments. The current director, Max Hollein, serves as a "curator, lawyer and diplomat" according to The Wall Street Journal, producing approximately 40 exhibits annually, managing around 2,200 employees, and supervising the collection and curatorial departments. The director currently reports to Daniel H. Weiss, the Museum's President and CEO. Historically, the director has enjoyed significant autonomy; for instance, Philippe de Montebello refused to report to then-president and CEO William Macomber in 1977. The director has traditionally held the role of president within the museum's leadership structure. On June 13, 2017, the Met announced the creation of a separate museum president, positioned above the director. Previous directors have included notable figures such as Luigi Palma di Cesnola, the U.S. consul at Larnaca in Cyprus and a Medal of Honor recipient; Sir Caspar Purdon Clarke, Director of the Victoria and Albert Museum; Edward Robinson, a secretary of the Art Commission of Boston and director of the Boston Museum of Fine Arts; Thomas Hoving, Parks Commissioner of New York City; and Max Hollein, director of the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco.
